panelText: Evaluation integrity and verifiable environments for AI agents.
panelDetail: Long-horizon reasoning · Reliable verifiers · Research to practice
bio:
I build and evaluate AI systems. My current focus is agent reliability: how to tell whether a system can solve a difficult task, and whether the test itself deserves our confidence.

My recent work includes coding-agent tasks, reproducible evaluation environments, and verifiers. I am interested in long-horizon reasoning, error recovery, and separating model failures from problems in the environment or grader. I am also exploring AI Neolab: an independent effort to bring mathematical and engineering talent to the design of better training and evaluation environments.

My background spans engineering and product development at Amazon, Boeing, and Carnival. I studied electrical engineering and earned an MBA from Purdue. Alongside my evaluation work, I build independent projects, including [ScienceToStartup](https://sciencetostartup.com) and SnoLocal.

projects.title: AI Neolab
projects.description: An exploratory effort focused on expert-designed training and evaluation environments for AI agents. The question is whether difficult tasks with independently verifiable outcomes can improve reliability on new problems.

projects.title: ScienceToStartup
projects.description: A tool for examining arXiv papers as potential startup ideas: what the research makes possible, where it might be useful, and what would need to be tested.

projects.title: SnoLocal
projects.description: A hyperlocal iOS planning app for families, built with SwiftUI and Supabase. I used written specifications, versioned project context, and AI coding agents throughout development.

Agent evaluation: constructing difficult coding tasks and checking that tests and verifiers measure the intended behavior.
AI systems and platforms: engineering and product work across enterprise AI applications, cloud infrastructure, and operational software.
Independent tools: building applications and research tools, including an AI-industry dependency tracker using SEC filings and news.
serviceText:
Evaluation integrity: reproducible tasks, robust verifiers, and distinguishing a model failure from a broken test.
Reliable agents: long-horizon behavior, error recovery, and performance on unfamiliar tasks.
Empirical AI safety: understanding consequential failure modes and testing whether proposed safeguards work.
Research to practice: turning promising technical ideas into systems whose usefulness can be measured.
noteText: Start with a concrete task. Define what success means. Test the verifier as carefully as the system being evaluated. Keep claims proportional to the evidence.
contactText: I am interested in conversations about reliable agents, evaluation environments, and research-driven products. You can reach me on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/musa-emin-ozdem/).
